issue_request: FHIR-20510 was Applied with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core ServiceRequest. It requested changing ServiceRequest.quantity[x] to the concise definition "An amount of service being requested.", moving the Quantity/Ratio/Range examples into a comment, and adding a ServiceRequest example that uses quantity.
initial_application: HL7/fhir#3119 appears to be the implementation. Commit 9e86b9f5cc042823a8e49032e2c115b5cc9f39ad changed source/servicerequest/structuredefinition-ServiceRequest.xml and added source/servicerequest/servicerequest-example-physicaltherapy.xml to list-ServiceRequest-examples.xml; merge e8dec40a561283d86e35da46e4f9c0681c7fba36 merged the work as changes for FHIR-20510.
additional_context: The original Zulip discussion asked whether ServiceRequest.quantity represents duration, total count, or a scheduled quantity. OO minutes on 2024-05-02 approved the Jira, and 2024-05-07/2024-05-10 minutes plus the Jira comment show follow-up discussion about example specificity. The current authoritative XML source is correct; source/servicerequest/servicerequest.svg still has the old tooltip text, but it is a generated-looking diagram artifact and not a source-only reason to edit under the run guardrail.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active ServiceRequest resource source already has the voted definition/comment and a build-scope quantityRatio example.
